claim_vs_prior_implication.reasoning: Published 2026 cyclic-dihedral uniform threshold is the specialization \(r_p=1\); the arbitrary-rank hyperplane incidence counts are not stated there. The 2019 theorem concerns minimum rather than uniform intersections. The related generalized-dihedral published findings concern minimal generating graphs or subgroup permutability, not incidence among all maximal subgroups. In particular the noncyclic \(A=C_3\times C_3\) gives \(\operatorname{ui}=5\), whereas the cyclic prime-power case gives \(\operatorname{ui}=2\), so the cyclic theorem does not directly cover the noncyclic claim.

value.rationale: The 2026 cyclic-dihedral uniform-intersection problem motivates a natural noncyclic extension. The theorem classifies the complete elementwise incidence profile, not only a single small count, for all finite abelian inversion kernels; its p-rank formula supplies a sharp uniform threshold for arbitrary mixed-Sylow and even-torsion families and explains the structural role of Frattini residues.
